title: LL6-050: six-input prefix composition lowers memory at the half-source point

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single LL6-050 algorithm and complete configuration of proof.md (finite branch n<2^32; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), z=ceil(log2 r), m=floor(19342r/100000)-10z, lambda=ceil(10341r/10000)+200z, kappa=ceil(log2(m+5))+3, full six-input widths5lambda-kappa, five binary remainder levels, explicit hard counters and both all-modulus decoders) recovers the full secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal copies. On EVERY execution branch including retries, failed attempts, discarded copies and aborts, total charged sequential work is T(N,s)=O(2^((4637/1000)sqrt n)). The exact uniform envelope B_T(n)=2^((4637/1000)sqrt n) has growth index1/2 and an absolute outside constant. The proof charges all six-list enumeration, source/extraction, classical processing, circuit generation, decoding, reset, initialization, measurement and addressing, and uses an exact rational logarithm certificate plus positive coefficient gaps to absorb polynomial factors. This holds jointly with the other resource and zero-tolerance claims for the same algorithm/configuration.

For the same LL6-050 algorithm/configuration of proof.md, every N>=2 and s, n=ceil(log2 N), peak classical allocation on EVERY branch is S_C(N,s)=O(2^((5171/5000)sqrt n)) bits, including retained full-label tables, bounded six-list prefixes, heaps, buffers, extraction scratch and streamed decoder records. The exact uniform envelope B_C(n)=2^((5171/5000)sqrt n) has growth index1/2 and an absolute outside constant. This holds jointly with full-secret success at least1-2^-8 and all other resource and zero-tolerance claims.

For the same LL6-050 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak quantum memory on every execution branch is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits, with an absolute constant, including the depth-first index registers and all ancillas. The envelope B_Q(n) = n has growth index exactly 0. This holds jointly with the stated work, classical-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LL6-050 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including every discarded copy and every failed or aborted attempt, is O(2^((1/2) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The main-branch hard cap is Q <= n Ccap + K = O(n^3 6^m), with Ccap,K,m defined in proof.md; the proved upper coefficient q*258497/100000 is strictly below1/2 and absorbs its polynomial factor. The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((1/2) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work and memory bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LL6-050 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
